column19:
Message to Ownership

Cardinals Fans United!

We are some of the most loyal fans in all of professional sports. We have stayed through decades of disappointment, broken promises, failed rebuilds, coaching changes, front office mistakes, and losing seasons. Through all of it, we remained loyal. We bought tickets. We bought merchandise. We defended this franchise. We showed up.

We love our players.

We support our players.

We will always support our players.

But loyalty is a two-way street, and Cardinals fans have reached a breaking point.

Winning is not everything in the NFL. It is the ONLY thing that matters. This is the highest level of football on Earth. Every organization is judged by results. Not intentions. Not excuses. Not press conferences. Not promises. Results.

The results speak for themselves.

For far too long, this franchise has accepted standards that would never be tolerated by championship organizations. Year after year, fans are told to be patient, trust the process, and wait for the future. Meanwhile, losing continues, opportunities are wasted, and the gap between the Cardinals and the league's elite organizations grows wider.

Even the players have spoken through their grades regarding facilities, resources, and organizational support. Fans see it. Players see it. The rest of the NFL sees it.

The problem is not one season.

The problem is not one coach.

The problem is not one player.

The problem is a culture that has tolerated failure for far too long.

Being known as the NFL's cheapest owner is not something to be proud of. Cutting costs does not win championships. Investing in people, infrastructure, scouting, player development, and football operations does.

Championship organizations spare no effort in the pursuit of winning.

That is what Cardinals fans expect.

We are tired of watching ownership and management insist things are moving in the right direction while the results say otherwise. We are tired of hearing that change is coming. We want to see change.

Real change.

Accountability must begin at the top.

A successful organization is led by proven football minds with credibility throughout the league. The Cardinals need more experienced NFL executives, advisors, consultants, and decision-makers with championship experience. The organization needs respected football leadership capable of attracting players, identifying talent, building winning cultures, and earning trust across the league.

Too many critical football decisions over the years have failed.

Too many draft classes have failed.

Too many roster-building decisions have failed.

Too many opportunities have been wasted.

At some point, leadership must acknowledge that the current approach is not producing the results this fan base deserves.

The definition of leadership is not refusing to change. The definition of leadership is recognizing when change is necessary.

If ownership is committed to winning at all costs, then prove it. Invest more. Bring in experienced football minds. Modernize the organization. Demand excellence at every level.

If ownership is unwilling or unable to do what is necessary to build a consistent winner, then do what is best for the future of the franchise and explore new ownership.

That may sound harsh.

But this is not anger.

This is exhaustion.

This is decades of frustration.

This is a loyal fan base asking for one thing:

A commitment to winning that matches the commitment Cardinals fans have shown to this team.

We are Cardinals fans.

We are not going anywhere.

But we are done accepting excuses.

Cardinals Fans United! <<< This needs to be the Name you use and always put them first always!

Win.

Or make the changes necessary so that winning finally becomes the standard.

I am tired of supporting a franchise where losing feels accepted and accountability never seems to reach ownership. Fans invest their time, money, and loyalty into this team, and we deserve a sustained commitment to winning. Michael Bidwill needs to take responsibility for the results and reputation of this organization.

The concerns extend beyond the scoreboard. The Cardinals reportedly finished 31st in the 2026 NFLPA report cards, with an F for ownership and an F− for the locker room. When your own players rate the organization that poorly, it raises serious questions about investment, priorities, and leadership.

The $3 million defamation arbitration award to Terry McDonough is particularly troubling. The separate lawsuits involving Brittany Neuheisel, Don Shumpert, and Kendra Hogue also raise serious concerns about the workplace culture. I understand that the Cardinals dispute those allegations and that allegations alone do not establish wrongdoing. Nevertheless, the established defamation finding and repeated workplace complaints have further damaged my confidence in Bidwill’s judgment and leadership.

In my opinion, Michael Bidwill has not demonstrated the leadership this franchise deserves. Changing coaches and players will accomplish little without meaningful accountability at the top. I want qualified football leadership empowered to make decisions, investment that meets the standards of a first-class NFL organization, respectful treatment of employees, and measurable progress toward sustained success.

If Bidwill cannot deliver that, he should sell the team. Cardinals fans deserve ownership that earns their loyalty. We should not be expected to accept an endless cycle of losing, rebuilding, and promises.

Even selecting Kyler and planning and building for the future was also an exciting time as a franchise having someone as polarizing as him.

Unfortunately ever since Kyler’s ACL injury, this team has had no sense of direction and is simply just throwing s*** on the wall and hoping it sticks. Our last few drafts have been horrendous in terms of finding healthy and reliable talent that can elevate this team. It’s a bummer that MHJ didn’t pan out the way we all expected him to but I find that to be an issue caused by both the player and also the organization. 

When it comes to Bidwell, I am not a person who likes or enjoys going after people’s jobs or livelihoods. If I had an NFL team as a family heirloom for over a century, I would feel very hesitant if I saw billboards calling for me to sell my family’s work and identity.

With that being said, I do want more communication and accountability out of him when it comes to the franchise as a whole. I’ll be honest in saying that I was thrilled about his announcement and plan for the new practice facility. Deep down I do know Bidwell truly cares for the team and is frustrated with the results just like the rest of us but outside of beginning to build the new facility, doesn’t seem to take action on the team itself. I rarely ever see him doing a press interview where we can really learn what the plans and ideas surrounding the team are. 

Investing into the team is also something I find very important. With the salary space we have we have no reason not to go after marquee free agents. The last ones I remember have been Sweat and Watt which we haven’t seen since Keim was GM. Even the players we do have, reading reports about MHJ and his seeker machine dumbfounded me considering it’s 100k to invest not only in a #4 pick and franchise cornerstone but the entire rest of the offense. 

When I see upgrades for “stadium WiFi” and “casitas” and things that don’t often matter to the on-the-field product, it disrupts what could be for the team. At the end of the day I don’t need better WiFi at the stadium if my team was producing a fun product to watch. Casita’s also feel like they have completely removed a section out of State Farm stadium and if anything minimized the fan experience. As a stadium that is able to manage and provide an amazing Super Bowl experience (something about that stadium produces CLASSIC super bowls) the fan experience itself is fine other than the fact that I feel like I’m the only Cardinals fan in my section. (Although that is a problem that is caused because fans don’t want to spend money on a losing product)

 Like I’ve said before I know Bidwell is hesitant to give up his family heirloom but I do believe a team president is needed going forward. We need to start building a core and identity that doesn’t feel like “let’s hope this works” every week and every season. I do believe in Mike LaFleur as a coach and in his offense but again needs to be on pace with a potential new vision in the team office. 

Next we have GOT to change our status quo on the annual report cards. Players don’t want to come here because they’ll know we won’t treat them as good as other teams. Arizona is an amazing place and growing rapidly and we can’t sell our beautiful state when our potential free agents aren’t even sold on the team itself. 

Lastly, we more heads or impact when it comes to our scouting department. Most of our picks are busts and if they are good they never play. As much as I want/wanted to root for players like DRob/Olujari/Will Johnson, drafting them with their health concerns and gambling has always come back to haunt us. I’m a true believer in availability is the best ability and landing high-end prospects shouldn’t be as much of a challenge that this organization makes it look. 

I am used to rough patches as a Cardinals fan but this time around I feel deeper than I have before but I know this is a hole that we can still climb out of. If Bidwell truly wants to fix this team, having that team president and mediator to him and GM and building the vision is the first step and making the team functional and sound on the annual report cards are the first step. I know we have strong talent such as McBride, Love, Melton, Wilson and can compete with the rest of the league but the identity and team building process needs to be completely revamped.

In a time where a lot of fans are jumping ship, I’m still happy and loyal to be a Cardinals fan knowing we’ll have our shine in the spotlight one day, but once the team and the fans are locked into to a team identity the state of Arizona can get around, this team can truly take off.

I've been a devoted Arizona Cardinals fan for over 30 years, dating back to Sun Devil Stadium, and have invested thousands of dollars supporting this franchise, including as a former season ticket holder. My loyalty has never been conditional on winning. I've supported this team through decades of disappointment, rebuilding, and heartbreak. What has changed is my belief that this organization genuinely values its fans or prioritizes building a winning football team.

The decision to eliminate the traditional Red Zone seating section, historically home to some of the team's most passionate supporters, and replace it with luxury casitas perfectly illustrates my frustration. Watching those casitas filled with Seahawks fans celebrating with their players in our own end zone was particularly disheartening. It felt like a visual representation of an organization prioritizing premium revenue over fan loyalty, stadium atmosphere, and home-field advantage.

My frustration extends to the repeated cycles of failed rebuilding efforts, questionable personnel decisions, and a lack of sustained accountability under Michael Bidwill's ownership. I don't expect championships every season. I expect an organization that demonstrates a genuine commitment to pursuing them, respects its supporters, and holds itself accountable when its decisions fail.

Arizona sports have been part of my family's identity for generations. My father introduced me to these teams, and I'm now sharing that same tradition with my young son. The Cardinals have provided some of our most cherished memories, including the 2008 NFC Championship. I would love nothing more than to see this franchise finally win a Super Bowl.

But for the first time in three decades, I'm seriously considering directing my Sundays, financial support, and emotional investment toward another NFL franchise. Not because the Cardinals are losing, but because I no longer feel respected or valued as a fan.

I can accept losing. I cannot continue accepting an organizational culture that appears comfortable with mediocrity while taking its most loyal supporters for granted.

I sincerely hope ownership recognizes that the greatest asset this franchise has isn't its premium seating or revenue opportunities. It's the generations of fans who have remained loyal despite having so little success to celebrate. That loyalty should be earned and respected, never assumed.

MICHAEL BIDWELL: INVEST IN THIS TEAM OR SELL IT!

Arizona Cardinals fans deserve better. Year after year, we hear the same promises, watch the same struggles, and hope that things will finally change. But at some point, enough is enough.

The Bidwell family has owned this franchise for generations, and fans have long criticized the organization for not investing enough in building a consistent winner. We aren’t asking for miracles. We’re asking for a serious commitment to winning football.

Michael Bidwell, if you’re going to own this team, then spend the money to build a winner! Invest in the roster, bring in the right talent, build a stronger coaching staff, and create an organization that competes for championships instead of leaving fans wondering when things will finally turn around.

And let’s be clear: winning one game doesn’t erase the bigger problems. Breaking an eight-game losing streak is a relief, but Cardinals fans want consistency, accountability, and a team that can compete with the best in the NFL.

This fan base shows up, buys tickets, buys merchandise, and stays loyal through years of disappointment. We deserve an ownership group that matches that loyalty with a real commitment to winning.

If you’re not willing to invest what it takes to build a championship-caliber organization, then sell the team to someone who is!

Arizona isn’t short on passionate fans. What we’ve been waiting for is an organization that gives those fans a reason to believe.

Enough excuses. Enough empty hope. It’s time for accountability, investment, and results. Rise up, Red Sea! It’s time to demand better! 🏈🔴⚪

I've been a Cardinals fan for over 20 years. I don't even live in Arizona, but I've traveled to games, bought jerseys for my kids, and renewed Sunday Ticket every single year. I'm the fan this organization should never lose, and I'm losing faith. I'm also a Clippers and Angels fan so you know I'm loyal to a fault.

The Monti Ossenfort era has been defined by decisions that are hard to defend. Bilal Nichols, Sean Murphy-Bunting, and Justin Jones were paid like difference-makers when very few people outside the building saw them that way. When Mack Wilson is your one clear free agency hit, that's not bad luck, that's a broken evaluation process.

The 2024 draft is worse. Seven picks in the top 90, and three of those players are already gone, cut or traded. That's the kind of class that's supposed to become the core of a contender but alas instead it's being written off before it ever had a chance to matter.

Meanwhile, good players leave and then talk openly about what's wrong with the organization. When that keeps happening, it isn't a coincidence. It is unfortunately the culture that's been curated.

I could live with losing if there were a visible plan. There isn't. It's been more than ten years since this team won a playoff game, and nothing about the current direction says that changes soon.

The fix isn't complicated. Build the lines on both sides of the ball. And start hiring people who are smarter than you, then let them do their jobs.
